buckets.title: Pinnacle Vector Algebra question-demand extension
buckets.badge_reason: The main difficulty is preserving representation meaning: quadrant-aware direction, scalar versus vector products, projection, and axial direction.

conventions.statement: Declare an orthonormal right-handed i/j/k basis before reading or constructing component products.
Angles recovered from components or dot products must be reconciled with signs/quadrant rather than accepted from an inverse-trig principal value alone.

scope.covers: Magnitude/direction/unit vector from components, dot product for angle/perpendicularity/projection, and cross product for magnitude plus right-hand axial direction in selected ExamSIDE questions.
excluded: Scalar/vector triple products and coplanarity determinants beyond the selected first slice.
Vector calculus, differentiation of vector fields, and coordinate-basis transformations.
General tensor or matrix treatments of rotations.

capabilities.action: Recover an acute reference angle from a known trigonometric ratio using inverse sine, cosine or tangent.
capabilities.success_criterion: Given a valid ratio in its domain, evaluate the corresponding principal acute/reference angle; Physics must still determine the physical quadrant/direction from vector signs.

capabilities.action: Reconstruct a vector's magnitude, direction and unit direction from signed Cartesian components.
capabilities.success_criterion: Compute the nonnegative magnitude, use component signs plus an inverse-trig reference angle to identify physical direction, and form a unit direction vector by dividing every component by the same nonzero magnitude.

capabilities.action: Use the dot product to test perpendicularity, recover an angle, or calculate scalar/vector projection.
capabilities.success_criterion: Compute A·B consistently from components or |A||B|cos(theta), interpret zero dot product for nonzero perpendicular vectors, and use the correct magnitude denominator for the requested projection.

capabilities.action: Use the cross product to obtain a vector perpendicular to two vectors with the correct magnitude and axial orientation.
capabilities.success_criterion: Compute A×B with signed components or |A||B|sin(theta), apply right-hand orientation, verify anti-commutativity and perpendicularity, and normalize when a unit normal is requested.

microtopics.title: Recover magnitude, physical direction and unit vector from components
microtopics.badge_reason: The main failure is accepting an inverse-trig principal angle without using signed components to place direction in the correct quadrant.
entry_assumptions: Pythagorean magnitude and inverse-trig evaluation are available through declared Mathematics bridges.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Magnitude discards signs, so valid direction reconstruction must combine a reference angle with the component sign pattern.

teaching_path.action: Write the vector in one declared i/j/k basis and retain every component sign.
teaching_path.output: A=Ax i + Ay j + Az k

teaching_path.action: Compute |A| and divide each component by that nonzero magnitude.
For 2D, compute a reference angle from |Ay/Ax| then place it using signs.
teaching_path.why_valid: Inverse trig supplies a reference value; signs supply quadrant.
These verify normalization and retained direction.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The calculator value atan(Ay/Ax) is always the physical direction angle.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A vector has Ax<0 and Ay>0. Can a raw principal arctangent alone identify its quadrant?
misconceptions.repair: Use inverse trig for a reference angle, then component signs for the physical quadrant.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A unit vector keeps the original magnitude.
misconceptions.repair: Dividing by |A| preserves direction but makes magnitude exactly one.

exit_task.prompt: A 2D vector has components (-3,4). State its magnitude, quadrant information needed for direction, and unit direction vector.

reasoning: Any inverse-trig reference angle must be placed in quadrant II.
answer.check: The unit-vector magnitude is 1 and multiplying by 5 restores (-3,4).

oracle.no_numeric_claim: Exact inverse-tangent decimal is intentionally unnecessary.

microtopics.research_contribution: ExamSIDE Vector Algebra repeatedly requires unit-vector notation and direction recovery; this makes the representation change explicit.

predict.prompt: A vector has components (-3,4). First or second quadrant?

attempt.produces: Magnitude, quadrant-aware direction description and normalized component vector.

rubric.criterion: Uses signed components to place the direction after inverse trig.
Divides every component by one common magnitude.

accepted: Magnitude first, retain signs for quadrant, then normalize.
rejected: Report atan(Ay/Ax) without a quadrant check.

route.ask: Which information did squaring remove when computing magnitude?
What must be true after normalization?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Teaching supplies the full conversion; reconstruction starts from information lost by magnitude.

boundary_test.prompt: Can a zero vector be assigned a unique unit direction?
boundary_test.answer: No; division by |A| would divide by zero and the direction is not unique.
boundary_test.confirms: Unit-vector construction requires a nonzero vector.

microtopics.title: Use dot product for angle, perpendicularity and projection
microtopics.badge_reason: Learners often memorize A·B=ABcos(theta) without connecting it to signed components or projection normalization.
entry_assumptions: Can represent vectors in one Cartesian basis and compute magnitudes.
microtopics.inferential_jump: One scalar can be obtained from component alignment or geometric angle, so perpendicularity, angle and projection questions share one model.

teaching_path.action: Write both vectors in one basis and compute A·B by multiplying and summing corresponding components.
teaching_path.why_valid: Orthonormal basis directions separate component contributions.
Sign and magnitude encode relative alignment.

teaching_path.action: For projection of A onto B use (A·B/|B|^2)B.
teaching_path.why_valid: The normalization makes projection independent of B's scale.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A zero dot product means one vector must be zero.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Can two nonzero perpendicular unit vectors have A·B=0?
If B is doubled, should projection onto the same direction double?
misconceptions.repair: No. Divide by |B|^2 so rescaling B does not change the physical projection.

exit_task.prompt: Let A=(1,1,1) and B=(1,1,0). Compute A·B and the vector projection of A onto B.

answer.check: A-proj_B(A)=(0,0,1), whose dot product with B is zero.

microtopics.research_contribution: ExamSIDE includes direct projection, perpendicularity and angle questions, so dot product is supported by real question demand.

predict.prompt: Two nonzero vectors are perpendicular. What should A·B be?

attempt.produces: A component dot product followed by the requested interpretation.
accepted: Compute dot first, then interpret zero/cosine/projection.
rejected: Treat dot product as a vector or omit the projection denominator.

route.ask: What scalar is unchanged if A and B are swapped?
What denominator prevents projection from depending on B's scale?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Teaching names the identities; reconstruction recovers them from invariance checks.

boundary_test.prompt: Does A·B=0 identify a unique perpendicular direction in 3D?
boundary_test.answer: No; many nonzero vectors can be perpendicular to a given vector in 3D.
boundary_test.confirms: Dot product gives a scalar constraint, not a unique new direction.

microtopics.title: Compute and verify cross-product magnitude and axial direction
microtopics.badge_reason: Determinant signs, operand order and axial direction create distinct failure modes beyond component addition.
entry_assumptions: Can read i/j/k components and normalize a nonzero vector.
microtopics.inferential_jump: A×B is an ordered axial vector perpendicular to the input plane, not another component sum.

teaching_path.action: Keep the ordered pair A then B and one right-handed basis visible.
teaching_path.why_valid: Changing operand order reverses axial direction.
The expansion produces a perpendicular axial vector.

teaching_path.action: If a unit normal is requested, divide the nonzero cross product by its magnitude.
Check zero dot products with A and B and reverse operands.
teaching_path.why_valid: Perpendicularity and anti-commutativity independently test the calculation.

misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: If A×B points +k, where must B×A point?
What fixes the sign of the normal to the A-B plane?
misconceptions.repair: The right-hand rule applied to ordered A then B fixes orientation.

exit_task.prompt: Given A=(1,0,0) and B=(0,1,0) in a right-handed basis, determine A×B and B×A.

reasoning: k is perpendicular to both inputs.
answer.check: Dot each result with A and B; both dot products are zero.

microtopics.research_contribution: ExamSIDE now provides direct cross-product and unit-normal demand, removing the prior no-demand reason for deferral.

predict.prompt: If A×B points upward, what happens after swapping operands?

attempt.produces: A signed cross-product vector with order and perpendicularity checks.
accepted: Compute ordered cross product, then verify perpendicularity/reversal.
rejected: Treat A×B as commutative or scalar.

route.ask: What changes if A,B order is reversed?
How can you test the result without repeating the expansion?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Teaching gives the component rule; reconstruction emphasizes order and geometric checks.

boundary_test.prompt: What is the direction of A×B for parallel nonzero A and B?
boundary_test.answer: The cross product is zero and has no unique direction.
boundary_test.confirms: Axial direction exists only for a nonzero cross product.

relations.expression: |A| = sqrt(Ax^2 + Ay^2 + Az^2); A_hat = A/|A|; tan(theta_ref)=|Ay/Ax|
relations.meaning: Cartesian components determine vector magnitude and normalized direction; in two dimensions a reference angle is placed in the physical quadrant using component signs.

symbols.meaning: Signed z component, zero in a 2D problem
Unit vector in the direction of A

conditions: |A| is nonzero before A_hat=A/|A| is formed.
For a 2D direction angle, component signs are retained to place the inverse-trig reference angle in the physical quadrant.

derivation.action: Compute |A| from the perpendicular signed components.
derivation.why_valid: Orthogonal Cartesian components form perpendicular legs.

derivation.action: Divide every component by |A| to form A_hat.
derivation.why_valid: Uniform positive rescaling preserves direction and normalization sets magnitude to one.

derivation.action: For 2D direction, combine atan(|Ay/Ax|) with component signs.
derivation.why_valid: Inverse tangent gives a reference value; signs supply physical quadrant.
derivation.output: reference angle plus quadrant -> physical direction

limits: If Ax=0, the 2D direction is vertical and should be read directly from Ay.
A zero vector has no unique unit direction.
checks: Multiplying A_hat by |A| must reproduce the original components.

relations.expression: A·B = AxBx + AyBy + AzBz = |A||B| cos(theta); proj_B(A) = (A·B/|B|^2) B
relations.meaning: The dot product links Cartesian components to angle and supplies perpendicularity and projection tests.

symbols.unit_or_domain: product of A and B units

symbols.meaning: Angle between nonzero vectors A and B
Vector projection of A onto nonzero B

conditions: A and B are expressed in the same orthonormal Cartesian basis.
The angle form requires nonzero magnitudes for both vectors.
The vector projection formula requires |B| nonzero.

derivation.action: Multiply corresponding components and add them.
derivation.why_valid: In an orthonormal basis, same-axis products form the scalar dot product.
The dot product measures relative alignment.

derivation.action: For projection onto B, scale B by (A·B)/|B|^2.
derivation.why_valid: The denominator removes dependence on B's arbitrary scale.

limits: The dot product is a scalar; it does not produce an axial direction.
A zero dot product is a perpendicularity statement only when the nonzero-vector geometry is interpreted.
checks: A·A must equal |A|^2 and be nonnegative.

relations.meaning: The cross product is an axial vector perpendicular to A and B; magnitude gives parallelogram area and orientation follows the right-hand rule.

symbols.unit_or_domain: product of A and B units

conditions: A and B are expressed in one right-handed orthonormal i/j/k basis.
The magnitude relation uses the smaller angle theta between the vector directions.
Right-hand orientation is applied to the ordered pair A then B; reversing the order reverses the result.

derivation.action: Write A and B in the same right-handed basis and preserve order.
derivation.why_valid: Cross-product orientation depends on basis handedness and operand order.

derivation.action: Evaluate the signed component formula for A×B.
derivation.why_valid: The expansion produces the perpendicular axial vector.
A×B must have zero dot product with both inputs and B×A=-(A×B).

limits: This relation is the ordinary three-dimensional Euclidean cross product.
Parallel vectors give the zero vector, which has no unique axial direction.
checks: Magnitude must agree with |A||B|sin(theta) when theta is known.
